title: 医用工学
subtitle: Medical Engineering
keywords: Biomarker 2.Immune System and Antibodies: biological information from outside 3.exercise 4.electromyogram and information 5.Blood
educationalGoal: The role of engineering in the medical and welfare field is significant. Given that, however, the development of technology to quantify biological signals and changes in biological components and an understanding of the life sciences are essential for such engineering. This course aims to understand how medical engineering has been established, valuing the technologies and biological mechanisms necessary for medical care and diagnosis.
advice: This course will be taught in a lecture format using handouts. The course will be based on the contents of the previous courses such as structure and function of the human body, structure and function of cells, neuroscience, and bio instrumentation, so it is necessary to review the contents of these courses. The details of methods and analysis of biomedical measurements in the field of biomedical engineering will be covered in "Biomedical Measurements", so it is recommended to take "Biomedical Engineering" and "Biomedical Measurements" at the same time. To promote understanding, it is better to take "Biomedical Engineering" and "Biomedical Measurements" simultaneously.
books: Textbooks:Unspecified Reference books:医工計測技術入門[朝倉書店](Japanese) Reserved books:Unspecified
requiredKnowledge: In order to take Biomedical Engineering, students must understand and review the lectures of "Basic Biology," "Structure and Function of Cells," "Biochemistry," "Molecular Biology," and "Cell Biology" in the second year of the course, starting from the first year. Biochemistry, Molecular Biology, and Cell Biology. If you are unsure about the level of your knowledge of these subjects, please review the handouts and notes of each subject. If you are not sure about your knowledge of these subjects, it is advisable to review them by using the handouts and notes of each subject.

achievementLevels.standard: To be able to understand and explain in words the names and measurement principles of diagnostic and analytical equipment used in the medical field. To be able to understand and account for the principles of the biology of diagnostic and analytical equipment used in the medical field.
